chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When the tray is placed, say 'In the name of Allah'. When you eat, say 'In the name of Allah, upon its beginning and its end'. When it is removed, say 'All praise is due to Allah'.

key_terms.الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ: All praise is due to Allah (expression of gratitude)
key_terms.الْخِوَانُ: The tray or platter on which food is served

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended prayers to recite before and after eating according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) codifies the ritual etiquette of dining by prescribing specific invocations at the start, during, and conclusion of a meal. It reflects the Shia emphasis on transforming mundane acts like eating into acts of worship through mindful remembrance of Allah, ensuring that sustenance is consumed with spiritual awareness and gratitude.
